evidence.title: Dog Jam
evidence.text: Dog Jam is an annual rock festival held at Ford Park in Beaumont, Texas since 2001.

evidence.title: Dog Jam
evidence.text: It is sponsored by local rock radio station KIOC Big Dog 106 and Bud Light.

evidence.title: Dog Jam
evidence.text: Previous bands to play there include Default, 3 Doors Down, Breaking Benjamin, Korn, Droid, Five Finger Death Punch, Hellyeah, Element Eighty, Shinedown, and Staind.

evidence.title: Dive Bar Tour
evidence.text: The Dive Bar Tour, sponsored by Bud Light, was a promotional tour by American singer Lady Gaga, in support of her fifth studio album "Joanne" (2016).

evidence.title: Dive Bar Tour
evidence.text: The tour visited three dive bars in the United States, on October 5, 20 and 27.

evidence.title: Dive Bar Tour
evidence.text: All performances were live streamed on Bud Light's Facebook page, as well as Gaga's.

evidence.title: Ulterior Emotions
evidence.text: Ulterior Emotions was an album released in 2002 by Budweiser as part of their "Bud Light Institute" advertising campaign.

evidence.title: Ulterior Emotions
evidence.text: The album was a giveaway available to purchase on their website.

evidence.title: Ulterior Emotions
evidence.text: Also, for a time, you could download the song "You're Beautiful (Can I Go Up North This Weekend?)"

evidence.title: Ulterior Emotions
evidence.text: on their website for free.

evidence.title: Ulterior Emotions
evidence.text: Lyrics were included with the album.

evidence.title: Bud Bowl
evidence.text: The Bud Bowl was a stop motion animated Super Bowl advertising campaign first aired in 1989, and sporadically during the 1990s.

evidence.title: Bud Bowl
evidence.text: It served as an advertisement for Anheuser-Busch's Budweiser family of beers.

evidence.title: Bud Bowl
evidence.text: It featured anthropomorphized Budweiser bottles playing a football game against Bud Light bottles.

evidence.title: Alex the Dog
evidence.text: Alex the Dog was the advertising mascot for Stroh's beer in the 1980s and precursor to Budweiser's Spuds MacKenzie.

evidence.title: Alex the Dog
evidence.text: At the peak of his career, Alex appeared in parades, on "Good Morning America", and the "Today" show.

evidence.title: Alex the Dog
evidence.text: He even inspired a series of toys, posters, cologne, shampoo and hand lotion.

evidence.title: Alex the Dog
evidence.text: Hip-hop artist Tone Loc referenced Alex the Dog in his song "Funky Cold Medina".

evidence.title: Bede Aircraft
evidence.text: Bede Aircraft Corporation was founded by controversial aeronautical engineer Jim Bede in 1961 to produce the BD-1 kit aircraft, which eventually became the American Aviation Corporation's AA-1.

evidence.title: Bede Aircraft
evidence.text: The company also created and produced a number of advanced kit planes including the famous Bede BD-5 (pusher propeller driven) and BD-5J (turbojet driven).

evidence.title: Bede Aircraft
evidence.text: The BD-5J has held the Guinness record as the World's Smallest Jet Aircraft for more than a quarter century.

evidence.title: Bede Aircraft
evidence.text: Versions of it saw use in various Budweiser commercials (the Bud Light Jet, which was lost in an inflight fire and crash unrelated to airshow work).

evidence.title: Bede Aircraft
evidence.text: The tiny jet also appeared in two James Bond movies; "Octopussy" starring Sir Roger Moore, and later in a cameo appearance, hanging from the wall of Q's workshop in "Die Another Day" starring Pierce Brosnan as Agent 007.

evidence.title: Alex Cross (film)
evidence.text: Alex Cross is a 2012 American action crime-thriller film directed by Rob Cohen and starring Tyler Perry as the title character and Matthew Fox as the villain Picasso.

evidence.title: Alex Cross (film)
evidence.text: The adapted screenplay was written by Marc Moss and Kerry Williamson.

evidence.title: Alex Cross (film)
evidence.text: This is the third film appearance of the character Alex Cross, the lead of a series of novels by James Patterson.

evidence.title: Alex Cross (film)
evidence.text: Cross was previously portrayed by Morgan Freeman in "Kiss the Girls" (1997) and "Along Came a Spider" (2001).

evidence.title: Alex Cross (film)
evidence.text: In 2010, Idris Elba was hired to play Cross, but was replaced by Perry.

evidence.title: Alex Cross (film)
evidence.text: Filming took place in 2011, and "Alex Cross" was released on October 19, 2012 in the United States and Canada.

evidence.title: Spuds MacKenzie
evidence.text: Spuds MacKenzie is a fictional dog character created for use in an extensive advertising campaign marketing Bud Light beer in the late 1980s.

evidence.title: Spuds MacKenzie
evidence.text: The Spuds MacKenzie mascot and campaign were created by a 23-year-old art director, Jon Moore.

evidence.title: Spuds MacKenzie
evidence.text: At the time he was working at Needham, Harper & Steers, a Chicago, Illinois, advertising agency.

evidence.title: Spuds MacKenzie
evidence.text: The dog first showed up in a Bud Light Super Bowl XXI ad in 1987.

evidence.title: Spuds MacKenzie
evidence.text: During the height of his popularity, large amounts of Spuds merchandise was available, such as plush toys and t-shirts.

evidence.title: Budweiser Frogs
evidence.text: The Budweiser Frogs are three lifelike puppet frogs named "Bud", "Weis", and "Er", who began appearing in American television commercials for Budweiser beer during Super Bowl XXIX in 1995.

evidence.title: Budweiser Frogs
evidence.text: They are part of one of the most well-known international alcohol advertising campaigns.

evidence.title: Budweiser Frogs
evidence.text: The first Budweiser Frogs commercial was created by David Swaine, Michael Smith and Mark Choate of DMB&B/St. Louis, but only after their ACDs made them pitch first.

evidence.title: Budweiser Frogs
evidence.text: The commercial was directed by Gore Verbinski, director of the first three Pirates of the Caribbean films.

evidence.title: Michael Roarty
evidence.text: Michael J. Roarty (August 24, 1928 – March 16, 2013) was an American marketing executive for the Anheuser-Busch brewing company.

evidence.title: Michael Roarty
evidence.text: He has been widely credited with turning Anheuser-Busch and its products, including Budweiser, into globally recognized brands through advertising.

evidence.title: Michael Roarty
evidence.text: Roarty created the advertising slogans "This Bud's for you" for Budweiser and "Weekends were made for Michelob."

evidence.title: Michael Roarty
evidence.text: He also oversaw the creation of the Bud Light ad campaign featuring Spuds McKenzie during the late 1980s.
